description: A source-critical history of Japan’s shinobi: Iga and Kōka, wartime espionage, Tokugawa service, ninjutsu as intelligence practice, women and the changing meaning of kunoichi, surviving manuals, and the modern ninja in theatre and cinema. Distinguishes documentary evidence, prescriptive techniques, imagined teaching examples, and later legend.

period.label: 14th–20th centuries · historical shinobi and later ninja image
period.note: The subject runs from early fourteenth-century representations through Tokugawa-era service and manuals, and later early-twentieth-century fiction and 1962 cinema. It is not a date of composition of the historical sources; earliest evidence does not establish an origin date.
